Here’s a strong, professional follow-up email you can send to **James Keppel** based on your meeting notes and agreed action items:  

---

**Subject:** Follow-Up: Serana Health Growth Partnership & Investor Readiness Plan  

Hi James,  

Thank you again for taking the time to meet and for such a thoughtful discussion about Serana Health’s growth trajectory. I wanted to follow up with a quick recap and next steps based on our conversation.  

**Summary of Key Points**  
• Our immediate focus is launching a **90-day acquisition campaign** targeting 60 new paying clients to strengthen investor positioning and validate the $1M funding milestone.  
• We’ll refine Serana’s **B2B messaging and case study framework** to highlight ROI and demonstrate investor-grade proof of concept.  
• The **AI-driven client acquisition system** will automate lead generation and qualification, starting with B2B outreach via LinkedIn and email to build momentum in high-value markets like Texas.  
• Our **phased sales strategy** includes integrating external closers with your team to optimize conversions while maintaining oversight and alignment.  
• The proposed **performance-based pricing model** combines a small upfront fee with a 10% revenue share (limited to the first year per client), ensuring shared accountability and cash-flow flexibility.  
• Once the initial 90-day targets are achieved, we’ll align on scaling operations, refining investor materials, and positioning for the next funding round.  

**Next Steps**  
✅ I’ll send over the detailed pricing sheet and closer team options for your review.  
✅ Let’s reconvene **Tuesday** to finalize the rollout plan and confirm the messaging priorities for the Texas B2B campaign.  
✅ Once confirmed, my team will begin onboarding, CRM integration, and message development (Week 1 of the 4-6 week pre-launch timeline).  

Our shared goal remains clear: establish measurable proof of scalability, investor confidence, and market differentiation that sets Serana Health apart as a true leader in integrated telehealth.  

Please confirm if **Tuesday still works** for your schedule, and I’ll lock in the call.  

Warm regards,  
**Bethany Gifford**  
Founder & Growth Consultant | New Era Intel  
[www.newerainel.com](https://www.newerainel.com)  
bethany@newerainel.com | (Your phone number if you’d like to include it)

---

Would you like me to make a **version tailored for investor forwarding** as well (something James can easily share internally to summarize your proposal)?

create a follow up email based off of these : Investor Readiness and Market Positioning
Launching a focused campaign to acquire 60 new paying clients within 90 days is key to securing the $1 million investment milestone (16:55).

Bethany emphasized the need for a clear, evidence-backed B2B strategy since 89% of healthcare investors require case studies and proven ROI before committing (07:54).
James acknowledged difficulty in producing B2B case studies but sees potential in leveraging existing B2C success stories to attract investors.
The goal is to demonstrate consistent client acquisition and partnership success to validate the business model for investors.
Bethany proposed a growth partnership model that includes refining messaging and branding to differentiate from generic wellness programs, which typically yield lower rates.
This approach aims to reposition Serana Health as a specialized healthcare provider commanding up to 23% higher rates than general wellness offerings.
James and Bethany agreed that the current marketing efforts, including SEO, are producing some traction but remain insufficient to meet investor expectations (17:28).
Bethany noted inconsistent ROI and lack of marketing expertise contribute to limited visibility among discerning buyers.
A stronger digital presence and targeted campaigns are crucial to raising Serana Health’s profile in the competitive telehealth market.
The competitive advantage lies in Serana Health’s 360-degree health service model, integrating nutrition, primary care, and wellness, unlike competitors who offer fragmented or generic solutions (13:34).
Bethany highlighted the uniqueness of Serana’s multi-provider approach, which positions them well for both B2B and B2C markets.
Messaging development and B2B presentation creation are priorities to clarify this differentiation to investors and partners.
AI-Driven Client Acquisition and Sales Strategy
Implementing an AI-powered multi-channel acquisition engine will automate lead generation and qualification, focusing first on B2B clients to maximize ROI and margins (22:46).

Bethany described a system that uses AI to identify, engage, and pre-qualify high-intent leads across platforms like LinkedIn and email, handing off only sales-ready prospects to Serana Health (24:18).
LinkedIn was identified as the primary channel for B2B outreach, targeting decision makers directly with personalized messaging powered by AI trained weekly to mimic company tone.
Bethany’s team handles initial conversations, with humans overseeing AI responses to ensure quality and escalate niche-specific questions to James, preserving personalized service.
James expressed concerns about poorly targeted outreach causing leads to be discarded, which Bethany addressed by explaining a typical campaign response rate of 30-40% with about 10% expressing interest, emphasizing the importance of volume and qualification.
Bethany proposed adding high-ticket sales closers to the team to manage deal closings, offering options ranging from an elite closer at $2,500–$3,000 monthly plus 10% commission to more affordable closers working on commission-heavy models (36:56).
James considered integrating these closers with existing outside sales resources to avoid duplication and optimize the sales funnel.
This phased sales approach allows James to focus on closing after initial qualification, improving conversion efficiency.
The campaign infrastructure will integrate tightly with Serana Health’s Profitable CRM, ensuring all leads and client data funnel into a HIPAA-compliant, centralized system for seamless tracking and compliance (15:30).
Bethany stressed the importance of HIPAA compliance in all systems due to health data sensitivity, noting her team’s experience with healthcare providers.
Email warming and domain reputation management are part of the setup to maintain deliverability and avoid spam filters, with current deliverability already at an impressive 99% on existing email domains (41:24).
Pricing, Revenue Sharing, and Risk Mitigation
A flexible pricing model combining upfront fees with a 10% revenue share on acquired clients incentivizes Bethany’s team while controlling Serana Health’s cash flow and aligning interests (56:03).

Bethany clarified that the 10% revenue share applies only to revenue generated from clients or partnerships directly brought in by her team, not company-wide revenue or equity (56:54).
James expressed preference for capping this revenue share to the first year of each client’s membership, avoiding perpetual payments.
Bethany agreed that revenue share terms are negotiable and will be tailored to make financial sense based on client lifetime value (estimated at $7,000 per patient) and contract types.
To reduce risk for Serana Health, Bethany committed to a performance guarantee: if the agreed client acquisition targets are not met within 90 days of campaign launch, her team will continue working for free until results improve (42:54).
This guarantee is contingent on Serana’s messaging and internal systems being ready and responsive.
James appreciated the risk reversal, emphasizing his need for measurable ROI before committing significant resources.
Alternative marketing options were discussed, including building an in-house marketing team with an annual budget around $150,000 and traditional marketing agencies, but both were seen as less flexible or effective than the AI-driven growth partner approach (49:57).
Bethany positioned her team as a growth partner focused on continuous optimization, weekly feedback loops, and real-time data-driven pivots, unlike typical agencies that deliver only static ads and reports.
Geographic and Market Segmentation Strategy
Focusing initial client acquisition efforts on Texas, especially the Austin, Houston, and San Antonio areas, aligns with Serana Health’s higher-value Restore program and physician licensing constraints (01:09:47).

James explained that the Restore program requires a licensed physician involvement, making Texas a strategic priority due to their CMO’s license and the market’s high wellness engagement (01:11:02).
Bethany confirmed the ability to run multiple targeted campaigns simultaneously and recommended keeping the number of distinct campaign messages to four or five to maintain optimization quality.
A nationwide campaign for the less physician-dependent Restore program would run in parallel with the Texas-focused high-value program.
Targeting all businesses in Texas was proposed, leveraging the state’s size and corporate density for B2B partnerships (01:11:48).
Bethany noted the importance of defining the ideal client avatar and core messaging to tailor outreach effectively.
This segmentation allows Serana to prioritize markets with the highest revenue potential while maintaining broader national presence.
Implementation Timeline and Client Management
A compressed timeline of 4 to 6 weeks is planned to launch initial AI-driven campaigns after onboarding, followed by ongoing optimization starting around week 7 (01:06:23).

Week 1 involves multiple discovery meetings to finalize messaging, define client avatars, and set up CRM and integration processes.
Bethany will serve as the primary account manager, providing a single point of contact for James while leveraging her technical team for detailed reporting and system management (01:07:08).
Weekly client calls every Friday will review campaign performance, discuss pivots, and align on next steps, ensuring agility in response to market feedback (34:14).
James indicated a flexible but cautious approach to timeline, needing to address other priorities before committing fully, with a tentative follow-up scheduled for Tuesday to reassess (01:19:19).
Long-term Vision and Partnership Alignment
Bethany and James shared a vision of scalable growth, with plans to revisit roles and team structure after reaching initial client acquisition targets and securing investment (19:32).

James plans to hire a director of marketing post-funding, who would work closely with Bethany’s team to continue scaling efforts.
The partnership model includes potential integration with investment brokers to ensure client acquisition efforts align with investor expectations and facilitate future funding rounds (01:13:49).
Bethany highlighted her experience working backward from acquisition firms’ requirements to prepare businesses for sale, suggesting a future exit strategy roadmap could be integrated into growth planning (01:14:59).
The collaboration aims to position Serana Health as an attractive acquisition target or major market player by building a strong pipeline of clients, partnerships, and proven ROI metrics.

Action items
Bethany Gifford
Send recap email summarizing the growth plan, competitive analysis, pricing options, and next steps discussed in the meeting (01:19:03)
Schedule follow-up meeting for Tuesday to discuss progress and decisions regarding marketing and sales strategy (01:19:54)
Prepare detailed pricing and service sheet for closer team and revenue share terms for James to review (01:18:45)
James Keppel
Review the recap and evaluate options for combining external sales closers with Bethany’s lead generation system; prepare questions for next meeting (01:19:38)
Coordinate internal discussions about marketing budget, sales integration, and investor alignment before next meeting (01:19:38)
Bethany Gifford & James Keppel
Develop targeting criteria and messaging for B2B campaigns, especially focusing on Texas market and corporate clients without wellness programs (01:09:58)
